server.instructions:
CandleStack is a lab for experiments on financial time series: a user uploads a trading model (Keras or ONNX), describes its input in a manifest and backtests it on market data, crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca, then compares the results and publishes the good ones.

You act as the user who signed you in, with an API key or by allowing you on CandleStack (OAuth). The scopes of that sign-in decide which tools work: read (everything that only reads), backtests, models and publish. Call get_me first to see who you act for and what you may do. A tool that changes data says so in its annotations.

A failed tool call answers a problem as JSON: its type (https://candlestack.tech/problems/<slug>) names what went wrong and its detail says what to do.

Docs for agents: https://candlestack.tech/docs/agents/ and for this server: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/. The resource candlestack://docs lists every docs page and reference.

tools.description:
Closed OHLCV candles of one instrument in one timeframe, in pages of at most 500. Use it to look at the price around a trade, check a period before a backtest or compute something the backtest result does not say; a backtest loads its own candles, so do not fetch them for it.

With start: the candles from start on, oldest first; while next_start is not null, call again with start=next_start for the next page. Without start: the newest limit candles before end; call again with end=next_end for the earlier ones. Stocks have candles of the regular session only (09:30-16:00 New York); missing candles are never filled in (gaps). Counts against a per-minute limit of candle requests; ask for a longer timeframe rather than many pages.

Data terms: crypto comes from Binance spot, stocks from Alpaca (SIP, every US exchange, 15 minutes delayed). Alpaca allows its data for the user's personal, noncommercial use only: use it for the user's analysis here, never publish or pass on the stock candles.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#get_candles

How the user's new backtests start, as saved in Settings, Backtest defaults (or the app's defaults): timeframe, period, direction (long only or both), the signal threshold, stop loss, fees, slippage and the benchmark. Use these for every setting of a backtest the user does not name, so it runs as the app would start it.

The settings come twice. As Settings shows them: `stop_loss_pct`, `fees_pct` and `slippage_pct` in percent, the period in days. And in the units start_backtest takes, to pass through unchanged: `period` (data.period, UTC epoch seconds), `decision`, `execution` (stop_loss a fraction, fee_bps and slippage_bps in basis points) and `benchmark_instrument` (the instrument of the buy and hold benchmark; null for the backtest's own). The timeframe is not an argument of start_backtest: a backtest runs at its model's.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#get_backtest_defaults

Makes a one-time link to upload a model file (Keras `.keras` or ONNX `.onnx`, at most 50 MB) into the user's models. You never send the file through a tool: the file goes from the user's computer to the link, either by running `command` (curl), or by opening `page_url` in the browser and dropping the file there.

Then call get_model_upload with the link's `id` to see how it went and get the new model's ID; give the model a manifest with set_manifest before backtesting it.

tools.description:
Starts a backtest of one of the user's models on one instrument and period. One backtest of a user runs at a time and up to 20 more wait in the queue, so it starts running at once or waits (queued, with its place).

The arguments are the body of POST /api/v1/backtests: model.id (one of the user's models with a manifest), data.instrument.id (<market>:<symbol>: a stock for a model of US trading hours, a crypto pair for one of 24/7) and data.period ([start, end) in UTC epoch seconds), and optionally decision (how the predictions become a signal: threshold 0 by default), execution (fills, stop loss, position size, fees and slippage) and benchmarks (buy and hold of the instrument, or of SPY, QQQ or DIA for a stock). The `setup` get_backtest answers has this shape, so a backtest can be run again with changes.

Units: execution.stop_loss and position_size are fractions (0.07 is 7 %), fee_bps and slippage_bps basis points (10 is 0.1 %), not the percent of the app's Settings. get_backtest_defaults answers the user's defaults in these units too (`period`, `decision`, `execution`, `benchmark_instrument`): pass them through for every setting the user does not name.

Answers its ID and status at once; the run takes from seconds to minutes. Then call wait_for_backtest with the ID until it has ended, and get_backtest for the results.

tools.title: Check a sweep

tools.description:
Starts a backtest for every combination of `base` (the setup of one backtest) and the values in `vary`: models (each model's manifest sets what it reads and its timeframe, so list models to vary those), instruments, periods and decision rules, 2 to 20 backtests. All go to the end of the user's queue, which runs one at a time, or none does. `metric` is the statistic the ranking orders by.

Answers the sweep: its ID, each backtest's ID, status and setup, and the progress. Follow it with get_sweep until `done`. The backtests are ordinary ones, with the sweep's ID.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#run_sweep

tools.title: Run a sweep

tools.description:
A sweep of the user: how many of its backtests are queued, running, finished and failed, each backtest's ID, status and setup, and once none is queued or running (`done`) the ranking, best first, by `metric` or else the sweep's own. Values that read the same in the app share a rank, and the best and the worst are marked as the Compare page marks them.

Call it again while it runs; a backtest takes a minute or a few. For every statistic of the backtests, compare them with their IDs.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#get_sweep
